lessons: Never repeat the title/hook question immediately after the opening; restating the setup (e.g. Potatoes, Guardrails, Ponds) causes drop-offs of 27-32% at the 10% mark.
Avoid filler transition phrases like 'They look like similar fruits' or 'They are not just there to look cool', which triggered major drops in Fruits (32.1%) and Car Windshields (31.0%).

Hook with extreme comparative claims or striking visual contrasts (e.g., 'older than the United States' or 'tuna red meat vs cod white meat'), which yielded the highest initial retention (1.21-1.85) and top benchmark scores.
Do not prompt the audience to pause or guess (e.g., 'Pause and guess...' lost 8.3% retention); keep the narrative moving forward without stopping the flow.
Deliver immediate narrative momentum right after the hook instead of diving into dry background statistics (e.g., stating sap is 98% water lost 33.3% of viewers at 10%).
worst_moment_types: Restating the title question or verbatim line early in the video
Generic fluff statements that add no new information (e.g., 'not just there to look cool')
Interactive pauses or explicit prompts asking the viewer to guess
Dense background explanation or technical preamble right after the hook
best_hook_types: Bold historical or scale comparisons (e.g., 'older than the United States')
Direct visual counter-intuitive contrasts (e.g., red tuna meat vs. white cod meat)
Strong personification or provocative danger statements (e.g., 'pineapple is literally eating you back')
